props.gloss_en: R' Yehuda: an animal held in partnership with a gentile is obligated in the firstborn (half its value to the priest)
the Sages: as long as the gentile's hand is involved, it is exempt from the firstborn
R' Yehoshua: both expounded one verse, 'all the firstborn' (Ex 13:2)
the Rabbis (per the stam): 'bechor' implies even part, so 'kol' was written -- [exempt] unless the whole is [Jewish-owned]
R' Yehuda (per the stam): 'bechor' implies the whole, so 'kol' was written -- even any part
alternatively: all agree 'bechor' implies the majority
one master [the Rabbis]: 'kol' comes to fill out [the whole]
the other [R' Yehuda]: 'kol' comes to detract
Rav Huna: gentile partnership exempts even if it is only in its ear
Rav Chisda: [partnership in] a part that renders it a nevela
Rava: [partnership in] a part that renders it a tereifa
they disagree over whether a tereifa lives
the tereifa view holds a tereifa does not live
the nevela view holds a tereifa does live
the Rabbis before Rav Pappa: no disagreement -- Rav Huna's 'ear' concerns the fetus, Rav Chisda's and Rava's the mother
Rav Pappa: for the mother too we require 'all your livestock' (Ex 34:19), and it is lacking
Rav Pappa: rather, there is no difference [between fetus and mother] -- they disagree in both
the Master: 'every first issue, the sheger of an animal' (Ex 13:12) -- whatever dwells in an animal [is sanctified], so nefalim are sacred though not viable
R' Yochanan: [gentile partnership exempts] even in a part whose loss is a slight blemish
the mishna (16b): a ewe that bore a goat of sorts, or a goat that bore a ewe of sorts, is exempt from the firstborn; if it has some of [its mother's] signs, it is obligated
R' Yochanan: [such an offspring] has a permanent blemish, to be slaughtered on account of it
the slight-blemish dictum teaches like Rav Huna
...to the exclusion of Rav Chisda [and Rava]
...and to the exclusion of Rava
the mishna (40a): its mouth resembling a pig's is a blemish
the mishna (40b): one eye large and one small [is a blemish]
a tanna: 'large' means as large as a calf's; 'small' as small as a goose's
the stam's answer: no -- [one large eye] is a blemish because it is 'sarua' (an overgrown limb), not because of the change
the mishnayot (43a/44a): these blemishes disqualify [a priest]; a person has additional ones -- both eyes large, both small
of a person it is written 'any man of the seed of Aaron' (Lev 22:4) -- one equal to Aaron's seed; in an animal, both large or both small is no blemish
Rava to the convert: no one is concerned with R' Yehuda's view that gentile partnership is obligated in the firstborn
Rav Mari bar Rachel transferred the ears of [his firstborn fetuses] to a gentile, yet forbade them in shearing and work and gave them to priests -- and his animals died out
why did he transfer the ears at all? lest [the priests] come to a mishap with them
why did Rav Mari's animals die? because he abrogated their sanctity
Rav Yehuda: one may inflict a blemish on a firstborn before it emerges into the air of the world
alternatively: Rav Mari knew to make a complete transfer; another would see him, do it [incompletely] thinking it is what Rav Mari did, and come to a mishap

supports.gloss_en: הכי נמי מסתברא, דתנן: יתר עליהן אדם -- עיניו שתיהן גדולות שתיהן קטנות; in an animal both large/both small is no blemish (3b.7), so if change were the reason both should be; אלא לאו משום דהוה ליה שרוע (3b.8)

deflected_by.gloss_en: לא, לעולם אימא לך משום שינוי, שינוי הוי מומא; both large / both small come from excess health or weakness, which would affect both eyes -- so the mishna's ruling does not show the reason is שרוע

objections.gloss_en: מאי שנא בו, דבעינן כל בכור וליכא? אמו נמי בעינן כל מקנך תזכר וליכא! -- the distinction between fetus and mother fails; אלא לא שנא
מאי שנא מנפלים, דאף על גב דלאו בני חיותא נינהו קדשי? -- if non-viable nefalim are sanctified, why should gentile ownership of a part vital to the fetus's life exempt it?

answered_by.gloss_en: התם כיון דלא עריבו בהו חולין קרינא בהו כל בכור; הכא כיון דעריבו בהו חולין לא קרינא בהו כל בכור -- the nefalim have no non-sacred admixture; here the gentile's share is one

objections.gloss_en: והאמר רב יהודה: מותר לאדם להטיל מום בבכור קודם שיצא לאויר העולם! -- removing sanctity before birth is permitted (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest)

answered_by.gloss_en: התם מקדושת מזבח קא מפקע ליה, מקדושת כהן לא מפקע ליה; הכא אפילו מקדושת כהן קא מפקע ליה
